# Question: strongest canonical-fitting shortcut

The strongest plausible rival is:

> For each panel, assign class `ceil(min(bounding-box height,
> bounding-box width) / 2)`, then output 8 where two panel classes are equal
> and 0 otherwise.

It fits both official training demonstrations. The live source-bound probe also
checks all three labeled canonical pairs available in this packet and reports
3/3 fits (`checks/bbox-rival-probe.json`).

## Exact generated disagreement

Final generator SHA-256:
`5512b58f4b9ac1412a83152b0aeb56883831475e35def04edd41c67eaae6e941`.
The generator emits this ordinary default-band input at seed `1701`, sample
index `0` (7 rows × 23 columns; input SHA-256
`ad2f0b3b181d0c62b5ca890e15a701efdf70bceb7c70dc8a876990f98305f128`):

The authoritative exact input is retained as
`checks/shortcut-witness/input.json`; rendered exactly, it is:

```text
00000009111111190000000
01000009111111190000000
11100009111111190000000
11110009111111190010000
11111009111111190111000
01110009000000090111000
00000009000000090010000
```

The intended onion depths are `[2, 3, 2]`, so the selected Racket rule
(`51d1d5e43d4d`) returns:

```text
8 0 8
0 8 0
8 0 8
```

The rival classes are `[3, 3, 2]`, so the rival returns:

```text
8 8 0
8 8 0
0 0 8
```

I checked the intended output with the supported command
`arcpuzzles apply`, retained in `checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json`; the rival
calculation and source facts are in `checks/shortcut-witness/rival.json` and
`checks/bbox-rival-probe.json`.

## Does the repaired generator emit such cases?

Yes—more strongly, every ordinary generated input must contain one. The final
300-lesson production census materialized 1,200 labeled pairs and found zero
ambiguities against this rival in either production order or all 1,200 query
rotations (`checks/lesson-census.json`). Named degenerate texture overrides are
lawful edge cases and are intentionally outside that ordinary-witness promise.
